t: For a fire policy issued for 10 months, the premium chargeable is
e: Short-period scale: 9 months – 85%; for a period exceeding 9 months the full annual rate applies.

t: Sum insured on stock is increased from ₹50 lakh to ₹80 lakh with 6 months of a 12-month policy remaining; the annual rate is ₹2.00‰. The additional premium is
e: Increase in SI is charged pro-rata: 30,00,000 × 2/1000 × 6/12 = ₹3,000.

t: Visible physical damage to insured property caused by striking workers during a strike is
o: Covered only under the Terrorism add-on
e: RSMD covers visible physical damage by external violent means including that inflicted by striking workers; cessation or retardation of work itself is excluded.

t: Damage caused to insured property by the fall of a rocket during missile testing operations is
o: Excluded unless the terrorism add-on is taken
Covered only under the Aircraft Damage add-on
Covered under the Missile Testing Operations peril
e: Missile testing operations is one of the 12 named perils of SFSP.

t: For a floater declaration policy on stocks, the minimum deductible applicable to each claim is
o: 5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹50,000
5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹10,000
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹25,000
e: Circular on minimum deductibles: floater and floater declaration stock policies carry 5% of claim subject to a minimum of ₹50,000.

t: Insured property valued at ₹100 lakh suffers a flood loss of ₹50 lakh. The insured spent ₹20 lakh to save property worth ₹15 lakh. The total claim payable (ignoring excess) is
e: Loss minimisation expenses are payable but only up to the value of property thereby saved: 50 + 15 = ₹65 lakh.

t: A claim is found to be fraudulent in one respect only. Under Condition 8 of SFSP,
o: All benefits under the policy are forfeited
Only the fraudulent portion is disallowed
The claim is paid after deducting a penalty
The policy is cancelled pro-rata but the claim is paid
e: Condition 8: if the claim is in any respect fraudulent, or loss is occasioned by wilful act or connivance of the insured, all benefits under the policy are forfeited.

t: An SFSP policy with sum insured ₹8 crore at a location suffers a fire loss assessed at ₹1,50,000. The compulsory excess deductible is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). For SI up to ₹10 crore per location the excess is 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹10,000; 5% of ₹1,50,000 = ₹7,500, so the minimum ₹10,000 applies.

t: If the insurer is unable to reinstate property because of municipal regulations affecting street alignment, under Condition 9 it is liable
o: To pay the sum insured in full
Only to pay the sum required to reinstate the property to its former condition had it been lawful to do so
To pay the full cost of a new compliant building
e: Condition 9: the insurer may reinstate in a reasonably sufficient manner; where regulations prevent reinstatement, liability is limited to the cost of reinstating to the former condition.

t: Property insured under both a marine policy and a fire policy is damaged by fire in a warehouse. Under Condition 4 of the SFSP policy, the fire insurer pays
o: Only the excess beyond what would be payable under the marine policy
The full loss, with recovery from the marine insurer
e: Condition 4: the fire policy does not cover property insured by a marine policy except for any excess beyond the amount payable under the marine policy.

t: Which statement correctly distinguishes RIV and MV policies?
o: Under RIV the premium rate is charged on the reinstatement value, whereas under MV it is charged on market value
Under MV policies reinstatement is mandatory within 12 months
Under RIV policies depreciation is deducted at claim stage
RIV policies can be issued for stocks but MV policies cannot
e: RIV: SI and rating on reinstatement value, no depreciation if reinstated within 12 months, intimation within 6 months; MV: SI on market value, depreciation deducted, reinstatement not mandatory.

t: For the Architects, Surveyors and Consulting Engineers' Fees add-on (in excess of 3%), the specified sum insured should not exceed
e: Section VIII rate table: fees add-on at the policy rate on a specified SI not exceeding 7.5% of the claim amount; debris removal add-on on a specified SI up to 10% of the SI.

t: The Loss of Rent clause limits the amount payable to
o: The proportion of the sum insured on rent that the period necessary for reinstatement bears to the term of the rent insured
12 months' rent irrespective of the term
The market rent of similar premises
The full rent for the indemnity period
e: Rent clause: payable only if the building is unfit for occupation due to an insured peril, limited to SI × (reinstatement period / term of rent insured).

t: The Molten Material Spillage extension covers physical damage to insured property caused by spillage of glowing molten material
o: Including damage to the containers from inside
Arising without the occurrence of fire, excluding the cost of the molten material itself
Including the value of the molten metal lost
e: The extension (the 15th add-on in the notes) covers damage from leakage/spillage of glowing molten material without fire, excluding the molten material and damage to containers unless caused from outside.

t: Under a declaration policy, the basis of value for monthly declarations is
o: Market value anterior to the loss
e: AIFT Rule 14(e): the basis of value for declaration is market value; losses are settled on market value immediately anterior to the loss.

t: A declaration policy is cancelled by the insured after 3 months (no claims). Provisional premium ₹10,000; short-period premium on the average declared amount works out to ₹3,000. The premium retained by the insurer is
e: Declaration Clause condition 6: on cancellation by the insured, retention is the short-period premium on the average amount insured up to cancellation or 50% of the provisional premium, whichever is greater.

t: Which of the following is permissible under a Fire Floater policy?
o: Issuing it for building and machinery
Ignoring the presence of kutcha construction at one of the locations
Charging the lowest rate among locations
e: AIFT Rule 13: floater policies are for stocks at specified locations under one SI; unspecified locations are not allowed; kutcha construction may be ignored; rate is highest rate + 10%.

t: A policy with SI ₹10 lakh carries an escalation clause of 20%. A loss occurs on the 100th day. The sum insured to be compared with the value at risk for average is
e: Escalation accrues daily at 1/365th of the specified percentage: 10,00,000 + 10,00,000 × 20% × 100/365 = ₹10,54,795.

t: A 24-month EAR policy with total premium ₹19 lakh is to be paid in instalments. The number of instalments and the first instalment are
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). n = (T − 6)/3 + 1 = (24 − 6)/3 + 1 = 7. First instalment = 0.05P + 0.95P/n = 95,000 + 18,05,000/7 = 95,000 + 2,57,857 = ₹3,52,857; other instalments ₹2,57,857 each.

t: The policy wording of the Standard Fire and Special Perils policy appears in which section of AIFT 2001?
e: AIFT: Section I general rules and regulations; Section II policy wording; Sections III–VII rating; Section VIII add-on covers.

t: A home owner's declared carpet area is 200 sq m at ₹50,000 per sq m (SI ₹1 crore). After a total loss by earthquake, the surveyor finds the actual carpet area to be 180 sq m. Under Bharat Griha Raksha the claim is settled for
e: Where the declared carpet area exceeds the actual, liability is restricted to the SI for the correct area: 180 × 50,000 = ₹90 lakh. Where the declared cost of construction is higher than actual, the accepted rate is honoured.

t: Under Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha, under-insurance is waived up to
e: BSUS and BLUS waive under-insurance up to 15%; Bharat Griha Raksha provides a complete waiver of under-insurance.

t: A perfect party wall between two compartments of a building should extend above the roof by at least
e: A perfect party wall rises at least 2 ft above the roof to prevent spread of fire; an ordinary party wall does not.

t: Standard turnover ₹20 crore, annual turnover ₹100 crore, rate of GP 30%, sum insured ₹15 crore, turnover during the interruption ₹10 crore. The FLOP claim payable is
e: Sum to be insured = 30% × 100 = ₹30 crore; SI ₹15 crore gives 50% under-insurance. Loss of GP = (20 − 10) × 30% = ₹3 crore; after average ₹1.5 crore.

t: Delay in Start-Up (DSU) insurance is a
o: Project-stage cover for financial loss from delayed commencement of operations
e: Construction-stage policies: CAR, EAR/SCE, MCE, ALOP and DSU; operational: MB, EEI, BPP, CPM, DOS, MLOP.

t: For an EAR policy with sum insured ₹8 crore, the maximum TPL cover that can be granted is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). For project SI up to ₹10 crore, TPL may be granted up to ₹1 crore; above ₹10 crore it is 10% of completely erected value or ₹10 crore, whichever is lower.

t: An EAR policy ends on
o: The date of expiry or the date of commercial production, whichever is earlier
The end of the defects liability period
The date of handing over to the principal
e: EAR ends at DOE/commercial production; CAR at DOE/handing over to the principal.

t: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'cost of erection' component of EAR sum insured?
e: Cost of erection includes specialist visits, supervision and excavation; pre-operative expenses such as consultancy and licence fees are non-recurring and need not form part of EAR SI.

t: Which extension is available under EAR/CAR policies?
o: Penalties for delay under the contract
Loss of profit of the contractor
Breakdown of erected machinery after handing over
e: Extensions include express/air freight, additional customs duty, surrounding property, CPM, maintenance covers, EQ, debris removal, TPL, loss minimisation, professional fees, off-site storage/fabrication, escalation and design defect.

t: During the storage period of an EAR policy, the excess for a theft claim (not AOG, fire or explosion) is
o: 20% of the claim with a cap of ₹3 crore
10% of the claim subject to a minimum of the testing period excess
e: Storage excess: 10% of claim subject to minimum testing-period excess for AOG/fire/explosion claims; ₹5,000 for other perils.

t: An EAR policy with SI ₹100 crore in Zone II has EQ cover on first-loss basis at 10% of SI. If the tariff EQ premium for full SI would be ₹5 lakh, the EQ premium chargeable is
e: First-loss EQ: 10% of SI attracts 40% of the tariff EQ rate, i.e. 40% × ₹5 lakh = ₹2 lakh (20% of SI would attract 50%).

t: Steam was introduced into a turbine on 10 June and the TG set was synchronised with the grid on 12 June. The testing period commences on
o: 12 June, the date of synchronisation, as it is within 72 hours of introduction of steam
10 June, the date of introduction of steam
The date of the first full-load run
e: Testing starts on the date of synchronisation provided it is within 72 hours of introduction of steam; otherwise on the date of introduction of steam.

t: A 24-month EAR policy (testing not yet started, claims ratio 30%) is sought to be cancelled with 4 months remaining. The cancellation request is
o: Admissible only with the principal's consent
Not admissible, since less than 25% of the period remains
Admissible, since 4 months is not less than 3 months or 25% of the period (6 months), whichever is less
Not admissible, since claims have occurred
e: Cancellation needs claims below 60% of reworked premium, unexpired period not less than 3 months or 25% of the policy period whichever is less, and testing not commenced.

t: A defective part (A) damages the machine it is fitted in (B), a connected machine (C) and surrounding property (D). Under DE2 cover,
o: B, C and D are payable
e: DE2 covers only surrounding property; DE3 adds the connected machine; DE4 adds the machine containing the part; DE5 adds the defective part itself.

t: The design defect add-on wordings available under EAR are
e: EAR includes DE3 in the basic policy; DE4 and DE5 are add-ons. For CAR, DE2, DE3 and DE4 are add-ons for faulty design and DE5 for material/workmanship.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: Under an MCE policy, loss or damage due to flood during erection is
o: Covered only if below 20% of the sum insured
Covered, and the condition of average applies
e: MCE combines marine all-risks and EAR cover; flood is covered and under-insurance (average) applies to the project values.

t: Which of the following property is excluded under MBD?
o: Gear boxes insured with the driven equipment
Dies, moulds, blades, cutters and exchangeable tools
e: MBD excludes belts, ropes, chains, tyres, dies, moulds, blades, cutters, tools, engraved cylinders, glass/ceramic objects, operating media, felts, sieves, fabrics, linings, packing and non-metal parts.

t: Under MBD, foundations of machinery are
o: Covered only under the CAR policy
Covered if their value is declared separately in the sum insured
Automatically covered at no extra premium
e: Per the question bank, MBD covers the foundation of machinery if its value is declared separately.

t: Refractory material of a 2-year-old furnace is replaced in an MBD claim at a cost of ₹5,00,000. The amount payable before excess is
e: Refractory material in boilers/furnaces: depreciation 20% per year subject to a maximum of 80%; 2 years = 40%, so 5,00,000 × 60% = ₹3,00,000.

t: In an MBD policy, the onus of proving that a loss falls within the scope of cover lies with
e: Under MBD the onus of proof lies with the insured; under the policy the insurer's liability ceases if a damaged item is kept in operation without proper repair.

t: Under Section II (External Data Media) of an EEI policy, which cost is covered?
o: Cost of replacing the data media and re-recording data from a back-up
Cost of regenerating data where no back-up exists
Loss of information due to magnetic fields without physical damage
e: Section II covers replacement cost of data media and restoration of data from back-up; loss by magnetic fields and regeneration of data without back-up are excluded; substitute equipment falls under Section III.

t: Under the BPP policy, failure of an individual boiler tube is
o: Excluded unless it results in explosion or collapse of the boiler
Covered under the surrounding property extension
e: BPP excludes failure of individual tubes unless such defect results in explosion or collapse; it also excludes fire, AOG, impact by vehicles, chemical explosion, overloading and wear and tear.

t: Which of the following is excluded under a CPM policy?
o: Loss or damage due to total or partial immersion in tidal waters
Damage by collision at the project site
Theft of equipment from the site
Damage by riot at the site
e: CPM exclusions include breakdown, consumables, internal explosion, road vehicles, underground machines (exclusion K), wear and tear, transit, war, abandonment in mines/tunnels, pay loaders on barges and immersion in tidal waters.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: The DOS cover with the FOES (Failure of Electricity Supply) extension can be granted only to cold storages that
o: Have stand-by DG sets or oil engines coupled to the compressors
e: DOS with FOES extension cannot be given to a cold storage without stand-by DG sets/oil engines; with FOES the excess is 20% of claim (min ₹20,000) after an 8-hour time excess.

t: Which of the following is NOT a factor in MLOP premium rating?
e: MLOP rating depends on type and age of machine, relative importance, spares availability, shifts, indemnity period, time excess and claims history – not on location.

t: Under the deductibles circular, for an IAR policy with sum insured ₹1,200 crore per location (PD plus BI), the material damage deductible is
o: 5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹25 lakh
5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹10 lakh
5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh
5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹5 lakh
e: IAR MD deductible: SI up to ₹1,500 crore – min ₹10 lakh; ₹1,500–2,500 crore – min ₹25 lakh; above ₹2,500 crore – min ₹50 lakh; the SI limit is combined MD + BI per location.

t: For an IAR or mega-risk policy with sum insured above ₹2,500 crore per location, the MLOP time excess is
e: Above ₹2,500 crore: FLOP 14 days and MLOP 21 days; up to ₹2,500 crore: FLOP 7 days (14 for petrochemical) and MLOP 14 days.

t: A crane of individual value ₹20 lakh insured under CPM is damaged in a collision (not an AOG peril). The excess applicable is
e: CPM excess for individual value over ₹10 lakh up to ₹25 lakh, non-AOG perils: 1% of SI subject to a minimum of ₹12,500; 1% of ₹20 lakh = ₹20,000.
